# Opportunities and Potential {#sec-opportunities}

::: {.callout-warning}
## Writing Status
Pre-draft · Owner: TBD. The brief below is the direction set by the teaching team; the owner will research and rewrite it.
:::

## What This Chapter Covers

What vibe coding opens up is not "coding faster." Someone who couldn't write a single line of code can build working software, and an expert can shrink the distance from idea to prototype to under a day. This chapter addresses that opportunity concretely. It organizes, case by case, what doors have opened for whom (non-specialists, domain experts, solo founders, researchers), how the economics of software are changing (the marginal cost of custom software, the emergence of disposable software), and what has become possible in education.

## Seed Questions

- To what extent is it true that "now anyone can build software"? What do the failure cases show?
- Is disposable, personal software (software for one) actually increasing?
- How have prototyping practices changed at startups and in enterprise settings?
- What kind of tool is vibe coding for researchers? (data pipelines, visualization, simulation)

## Research Pointers

- Collect examples of non-developers building things (domestic and international communities, Product Hunt-type sites)
- Reports estimating the size of the vibe coding industry (figures must always be checked against primary sources)
- Use each student's first vibe coding experience as case data
